questions.stem: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Velocity is a vector quantity because it has both magnitude (speed) and direction. Mass, temperature, and energy are all scalar quantities that have magnitude only.

questions.stem: What is the key difference between a scalar and a vector?

options.text: Scalars are always larger than vectors
Vectors have both magnitude and direction, while scalars have magnitude only
Scalars can be negative but vectors cannot
Vectors are only used in advanced physics

questions.explanation: The fundamental difference is that scalar quantities are fully described by their magnitude (size) alone, while vector quantities require both a magnitude and a direction to be fully described.
